# Ghost

- Category: complement (publishing, memberships, community) — also available as an open-source, self-hosted platform
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://ghost.org/docs/ (redirects to https://docs.ghost.org/), https://ghost.org/help/, https://ghost.org/pricing/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md). **Where this file and `vendors.md` differ, `vendors.md` is authoritative.**

Ghost documents no formal "submit for review/approval" gate or notification when a draft is ready — third-party sources confirm publishers work around this with manual tags (e.g. #needs-edits, #ready-to-publish). | api_export         | Ghost has two public REST APIs: the **Content API** (read-only, public data — posts, pages, authors, tags, tiers, settings; authenticated via a query-param key safe for client-side use; explicitly "fully cachable" with no documented rate limit) and the **Admin API** (read/write — posts, pages, tags, tiers, newsletters, offers, members, images, themes, webhooks; authenticated via short-lived JWTs minted from an id:secret Admin API key, or staff/session tokens; no documented rate limit). Webhooks cover events like post.published/unpublished/added/edited/deleted, member.added/edited/deleted, user.added/edited/deleted, and site.changed, managed via POST/PUT/DELETE on `/admin/webhooks/`. Bulk export: a JSON export (mirrors the DB schema; includes settings, staff users, posts, pages, tags) via Settings → Advanced → Import/Export, and a separate CSV member export; **images/media are not included** in the JSON export and must be migrated separately. Import: the JSON format can be re-imported into another Ghost instance. | [Admin API](https://docs.ghost.org/admin-api) (2026-09-26); [Content API](https://docs.ghost.org/content-api) (2026-09-26); [Webhooks overview](https://docs.ghost.org/admin-api/webhooks/overview) (2026-09-26); [Exporting content and data](https://ghost.org/help/exports/) (2026-09-26) |
| custom_domains     | Ghost(Pro) supports mapping a custom domain (subdomain recommended, root domain possible but "non-standard") via CNAME/A records, with automatic SSL; only the Owner can activate it. The custom-domains help page makes **no mention** of whether this extends to the RSS feed URL specifically, nor of 301 feed-redirect support for leaving the platform — undocumented on this page. Self-hosted Ghost, being under your own infrastructure, has full DNS control by nature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [Adding a custom domain](https://ghost.org/help/using-custom-domains/) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| pricing_2_show     | Ghost(Pro) supports only **one site per account**, so the scenario's "2 shows" cannot be covered by a single published plan — this alone forces a workaround (two separate subscriptions) or self-hosting. Ignoring the multi-show constraint, a single show fitting the scenario (weekly audio/video content, ~10k downloads/mo is not a Ghost-billed metric, 3 staff seats, 1 premium/private feed) would need the **Publisher plan at $29/mo** (billed yearly; 3 staff users, paid subscriptions/premium tiers, custom themes) — Starter is excluded because it has only 1 staff seat and no paid-subscription support. For 2 full shows on Ghost(Pro), the realistic published cost is **2× Publisher ≈ $58/mo**, or self-hosting (MIT-licensed, free software; ~$15–80/mo in server/domain/email costs per third-party estimates) run as two site instances. Note: Ghost(Pro) pricing shown is the annual-billing rate; Ghost does not publish monthly-billing figures on this page.                                                                           | [Pricing](https://ghost.org/pricing/) (2026-09-26); (third-party) [Self-Host Ghost CMS: The Complete Guide](https://www.dreamhost.com/blog/ghost-self-hosted/) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                  |

## Integration surface

- **API:** Content API (read-only, key-in-query-string auth, exposes posts/pages/authors/tags/tiers/settings, no documented rate limit, versioned via `Accept-Version` header) and Admin API (read/write via JWT minted from an Admin API key, or staff/session tokens; covers posts, pages, tags, tiers, newsletters, offers, members (read), images, themes, webhooks; no documented rate limit). [Admin API](https://docs.ghost.org/admin-api) (2026-09-26), [Content API](https://docs.ghost.org/content-api) (2026-09-26).
- **Webhooks:** Event-based (post.published/unpublished/added/edited/deleted, member.added/edited/deleted, user.added/edited/deleted, site.changed), configured via Admin UI or `/admin/webhooks/` endpoints; 2xx response = success delivery. [Webhooks overview](https://docs.ghost.org/admin-api/webhooks/overview) (2026-09-26).
- **Export formats:** JSON (settings, staff, posts, pages, tags — mirrors DB schema, re-importable to another Ghost instance) and separate CSV for members. Media/images are **not** included in the JSON export. [Exporting content and data](https://ghost.org/help/exports/) (2026-09-26).
- **SSO / auth:** SSO is called out only on the **Custom (enterprise, unpublished-price)** Ghost(Pro) tier; undocumented for Starter/Publisher/Business or for self-hosted (self-hosted would rely on your own reverse-proxy/IdP setup, undocumented by Ghost itself). [Pricing](https://ghost.org/pricing/) (2026-09-26).
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) One site per account/instance — no native multi-show network layer, so a multi-show operation must run parallel subscriptions or parallel self-hosted instances. (2) No native transcripts, DAI, or podcast-specific analytics/IAB certification — these require third-party integrations (e.g. Transistor) layered on top, meaning podcast-specific data lives outside Ghost. (3) Content export excludes media files, so a full migration requires separately retrieving uploaded audio/video/images. (4) No documented approval/review workflow — editorial control is enforced only by role, not a publish gate, so any "immutable release record" requirement would need to be built externally. Self-hosting (MIT license) mitigates platform lock-in itself but shifts operational burden to the operator. | [Pricing](https://ghost.org/pricing/) (2026-09-26); [Exporting content and data](https://ghost.org/help/exports/) (2026-09-26); [What permissions do staff users have?](https://ghost.org/help/managing-staff-user-profiles/) (2026-09-26).

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Ghost is a strong fit for Relay's membership/community and premium-feed needs (native paid tiers, native commenting, and an official Transistor integration that syncs members-only podcast access automatically) and is fully portable (MIT-licensed self-host option, open JSON/CSV export, open REST APIs). It is weak everywhere Relay needs multi-show network structure: Ghost is strictly one site per account/instance, with no bundled multi-show billing or cross-show reporting. It has no enforced editorial approval workflow (only role-based publish permissions, patched via tags/process, not a platform gate), no native transcripts (DIY via code injection), no native video hosting or documented Apple HLS video partner status, and no documented DAI/programmatic ads or IAB measurement certification — podcast-specific plumbing must be bolted on via third-party hosts. Best read as a membership/website/community layer _in front of_ a real podcast host, not a replacement for one.

## Research notes

- `https://ghost.org/docs/` 301-redirects to `https://docs.ghost.org/`; fetched the latter.
- The Custom (enterprise) Ghost(Pro) tier is unpublished-price/contact-sales — flagged per brief instructions (enterprise-only pricing).
- Apple's HLS video partner announcements are dated Feb–Mar 2026 (post-cutoff, current per today's date 2026-09-26); Ghost was not named in any partner list found, and Ghost's own docs never mention Apple Podcasts video at all — treated as "not documented" rather than "not supported" since Ghost's docs don't address it directly.
- IAB Tech Lab certification: could not load the IAB's live certified-companies list page directly (search results only surfaced individual certificate PDFs for other vendors); relied on the absence of any Ghost-specific certificate and Ghost's own silence on the topic. Treated as undocumented per the brief's rule, not "not supported."
- Custom-domain-to-RSS-feed applicability and 301 feed-redirect-on-departure were not addressed by Ghost's custom domains help page; both left as undocumented rather than assumed.
- Self-hosted cost figures ($15–80/mo) are a third-party estimate (DreamHost blog), not from Ghost's own docs — labeled accordingly; Ghost's own pricing page only covers Ghost(Pro) managed hosting.
- Did not sign up, contact sales, or submit any forms; all findings from public docs/help/pricing pages and web search of third-party commentary where Ghost's own docs were silent.
